subject.title: Add dependency scanning for package releases

question: Should a high-confidence OSV `MAL-*` match automatically mark the exact package release malicious and block downloads, while allowing a manual approval made after that scan to restore it?
rationale: This changes the repository's install-blocking trust boundary and the authority of an external advisory provider; tests can prove mechanics but cannot determine the intended enforcement and override policy.

options.title: Approve exact-release enforcement
options.body: Accept automatic blocking for high-confidence OSV malware matches, retain post-scan manual restoration, and require live deploy, backfill, and outage proof before merge.

options.title: Stage advisory-only first
options.body: Persist and surface malware findings without changing download trust until production observations establish false-positive, retry, and moderation behavior.

options.title: Require manual quarantine
options.body: Use dependency findings only to create moderator work and never let OSV data directly set install-blocking trust.

recommendation.title: Approve exact-release enforcement
recommendation.body: Accept automatic blocking for high-confidence OSV malware matches, retain post-scan manual restoration, and require live deploy, backfill, and outage proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects Peter to existing scanner and moderation security boundaries rather than only this proposed implementation.
